name: The Sea and Cake
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: A painter, a cartoonist, a photographer and the busiest drummer in Chicago, named after a deliberately bent Gastr del Sol song title, making the lightest-sounding records of the post-rock years.

eras.title: Out of Shrimp Boat and The Coctails
eras.text: Before the band there were two cult Chicago acts: Shrimp Boat, with Sam Prekop and Eric Claridge, and The Coctails, with Archer Prewitt. When both wound down, the art-school friends found a drummer who was already in Tortoise.

years.h: Sam Prekop and Eric Claridge start Shrimp Boat in Chicago
years.p: With Ian Schneller, David Kroll and later Brad Wood, Shrimp Boat makes seven releases for labels including Bar/None and Rough Trade before 1993.

years.h: Archer Prewitt co-founds The Coctails
years.p: The Coctails move from Kansas City to Chicago after their 1989 debut and make six albums before a last show on New Year's Eve 1995.

years.h: Archer Prewitt starts Sof' Boy while coloring for Marvel
years.p: Prewitt self-publishes the Sof' Boy mini-comics while working as a colorist for Marvel Comics. In 1998 he is nominated for an Eisner Award for Best Colorist.

years.cap: The Sea and Cake · via Discogs
years.h: Shrimp Boat ends; The Sea and Cake begins
years.p: After Shrimp Boat dissolves in 1993, Sam Prekop and Eric Claridge recruit Archer Prewitt and Tortoise drummer [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]].

years.h: The name: a Gastr del Sol song title, bent on purpose
years.p: The band's name is a willful misreading of The C in Cake, a song by McEntire's other band [[Gastr del Sol|8f54d90b-f322-4e5d-a0fd-bdc960f2d20f]].

eras.title: Three albums in two years
eras.text: Thrill Jockey put out The Sea and Cake's first three records in quick succession. Claridge painted the covers and Prekop took the photos, and by 1997 McEntire was building the songs in a computer.

years.h: The Sea and Cake · Thrill Jockey
years.p: The debut sets the template: Sam Prekop's soft, half-sung vocals over interlocking guitars and McEntire's light jazz drumming.

years.h: Sam Prekop designs the cover of Tortoise's debut
years.p: The Sea and Cake's singer does the sleeve for [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]]'s first album, also on Thrill Jockey. The two bands share McEntire for the next thirty years.

years.h: Nassau · the second album
years.p: The first of two Sea and Cake albums released in 1995.

years.h: The Biz · the third album in two years
years.p: The Sea and Cake's second album of 1995, completing a run of three records in about two years.

years.h: The Fontana goes on Red Hot + Bothered
years.p: The band gives the song to the Red Hot Organization's AIDS benefit album.

years.h: Glad You're Right: a 7-inch in 500 copies
years.p: Lissy's Records presses the single, backed with Tiger Panther and Crimson Wing, in an edition of 500.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Sea and Cake · Wikipedia: John McEntire · Wikipedia: Archer Prewitt
years.h: The Fawn: drum machines, synths and John McEntire's first Pro Tools record
years.p: On its fourth album the band adds drum machines and synthesizers to the jazz, samba and bossa nova. McEntire, an early Pro Tools user, first uses it here.
years.xp: The same year brought Two Gentlemen, a 12-inch of mostly remixes, and A Brief Historical Retrospective, a Japan-only compilation. Prewitt also released his first solo album, In the Sun.

eras.title: Solo records and Bowie
eras.text: Everyone had somewhere else to be: Prekop made a solo record with Jim O'Rourke, Prewitt made three, McEntire ran Soma and Tortoise. The band still came back together for Oui and One Bedroom.

years.h: Sam Prekop's solo debut, produced by Jim O'Rourke
years.p: A soft, Brazilian-leaning record with Josh Abrams, Chad Taylor and Archer Prewitt.

years.h: Window Lights for Hefty and a soundtrack
years.p: The single Window Lights, backed with Setup for Bed, comes out on Hefty Records and lands on the Reach the Rock soundtrack.

years.h: Oui · the fifth album
years.p: The Sea and Cake's first album in three years, after a stretch of solo work.

years.h: One Bedroom · with a cover of Bowie's Sound and Vision
years.p: Recorded at McEntire's Soma, the sixth album ends with David Bowie's Sound and Vision, with singing by John and Frank Navin. It reaches 16 on Billboard's independent chart.
years.xp: Mikael Jorgensen of [[Wilco|9e53f84d-ef44-4c16-9677-5fd4d78cbd7d]] plays electric piano on some tracks. Pitchfork gave it 7.0.

years.h: The Glass EP
years.p: A CD EP closes the band's first decade.

eras.title: A break, then a rock record
eras.text: The band stopped in 2004 and came back three years later louder, recording in a Michigan studio. Then came four records in six years, all with Claridge's paintings or Prekop's photos on the cover.

years.h: The Sea and Cake goes on hiatus
years.p: After ten years and six albums, the band stops. Prekop, Prewitt and McEntire keep working on solo records, comics, Tortoise and production.

years.src: Wikipedia: Everybody (The Sea and Cake album)
years.h: Everybody: the Sea and Cake comeback, cut in Benton Harbor
years.p: Recorded at Key Club in Benton Harbor, Michigan, and at Soma, the seventh album was called the most rock-based record the band had made by PopMatters.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Jason Crock gave it 7.6, arguing the band stayed relevant simply by becoming more transparent. It reached number 9 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.

years.h: Car Alarm · the eighth album
years.p: The second album since the 2007 comeback, a year after Everybody.

years.h: Live at the Metro, officially bootlegged
years.p: Metro: The Official Bootleg Series, Volume 1 documents the band live at the Chicago club.

q: uniquely inventive blend of lilting pop and obtuse art-rock
years.h: The Moonlight Butterfly · a short one
years.p: A compact record that Mojo's David Sheppard used to sum up the band.
years.xp: Sheppard's review ran in Mojo's July 2011 issue.

years.h: Runner · Eric Claridge's last album with the band
years.p: The tenth album is the last to feature bassist and cover painter Eric Claridge.

eras.title: Down to three
eras.text: Without Claridge, the band wrote as a trio for the first time and brought Doug McCombs of Tortoise along on bass for shows. The shared-drummer Chicago family got smaller and closer.

years.src: Thrill Jockey: The Sea and Cake · Wikipedia: Doug McCombs
years.h: Eric Claridge is gone; the Sea and Cake becomes a trio
years.p: Any Day is the first Sea and Cake album without founding bassist Eric Claridge. Thrill Jockey says the trio found writing as a smaller unit inspiring.
years.xp: Doug McCombs of [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]] and [[Brokeback|e3fa3b7a-b883-4432-9152-ed0cf4d5c19c]] joins as touring bassist from May 2018. No public reason for Claridge's exit appears in the sources.

years.h: Any Day · stacked guitars, organs, a flute
years.p: The eleventh album has Paul Von Mertens on flute and clarinet and Nick Macri on double bass, and Sam Prekop's most vocal-centered songs. The Guardian called it elegantly disheveled jazz rock.

years.h: Sam Prekop and John McEntire make Sons Of
years.p: Two thirds of the band release a duo album built on modular synthesizers, Prekop's focus since Old Punch Card in 2010.
